title: [Crop And Lock] Reparent mode shows a different region than the crop (browser windows)
author: CM-idea
summary: Crop And Lock Reparent mode can show an offset region for maximized Chromium windows while hit-testing still targets the selected source area.

status.label: Detailed design candidate
status.detail: The report gives a deterministic browser/maximized-window repro and the reparent implementation has a bounded coordinate-space path to investigate.

next_action.label: Queue a focused implementation-grade design investigation.
next_action.reason: Queue this issue for detailed design; a maintainer can also reproduce the maximized-browser reparent offset locally.

judgment.rationale: The public report is specific enough to start a focused design investigation: Reparent mode offsets the displayed region for maximized Edge/Chrome windows, Thumbnail mode is unaffected, and input hit-testing still maps to the original intended content. Source inspection shows Reparent mode has its own maximized-window adjustment before SetParent/SetWindowPos, while Thumbnail mode uses a different DWM thumbnail crop path.
evidence: The issue reports PowerToys 0.101.2362, GitHub install, Windows 11 Pro build 26200, user install, admin run, and Edge 153.0.4234.32.

Reported reproduction: maximize a Chromium browser, start Crop And Lock Reparent mode, crop a browser region such as a video player, and compare the resulting Crop And Lock window to the selected region.
Reported result: the Reparent window shows a completely different region with a large offset, but mouse hit-testing still lands where the content would be in the original window.
Reported contrast: Thumbnail mode is unaffected because it does not touch the source window, and File Explorer almost never shows the issue.

Focused source review: OverlayWindow records crop rectangles relative to ClientAreaInScreenSpace; ReparentCropAndLockWindow then adjusts those coordinates with a special maximized-window branch using monitor work-area offsets before reparenting the source HWND; ThumbnailCropAndLockWindow uses a DWM thumbnail source rectangle instead.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue this issue for detailed design and reproduce it against a maximized Chromium window before choosing the fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix is plausible in the Crop And Lock reparent coordinate path, and no existing linked fix attempt or duplicate is visible in the current issue.

issue_context.summary: A maximized Chromium browser cropped with Crop And Lock Reparent mode displays a different offset region than the selected crop, while clicks still hit the selected source area. Thumbnail mode does not show the problem.
known_information: PowerToys version 0.101.2362 from GitHub is affected.
The reporter reproduced with Microsoft Edge 153.0.4234.32 on Windows 11 Pro build 26200.
The source window is maximized before using Reparent mode.
The visible output is offset by a large amount, but mouse hit-testing still maps to the selected original content.
Thumbnail mode is unaffected, and File Explorer almost never shows the behavior.
The issue currently has no comments and no linked fix or duplicate in the live metadata.
inferences: The display/input asymmetry suggests the source HWND is being reparented and positioned in a coordinate space that does not match the selected client-area crop.
The browser/maximized-window specificity points to non-client frame, work-area, or client-origin handling in Reparent mode rather than the overlay selection itself.
Because Thumbnail mode uses DWM thumbnail source rectangles and is unaffected, the defect is likely isolated to the Reparent mode SetParent/SetWindowPos coordinate conversion.
issue_context.analysis: The report already supplies the version, app type, maximized-window precondition, expected and actual behavior, and a mode comparison. A maintainer-side reproduction is more useful than asking the reporter for generic logs. The next useful step is an implementation-grade design pass that instruments and compares OverlayWindow's client-relative crop rectangle, ReparentCropAndLockWindow's maximized adjustment, the Chromium client origin, and the final child-window offset.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete live issue body, labels, author, updatedAt, and empty comment thread through 2026-09-20T21:09:11Z.
Read Crop And Lock source in OverlayWindow.cpp, ReparentCropAndLockWindow.cpp, ThumbnailCropAndLockWindow.cpp, WindowRectUtil.h, and CropAndLockTests.cs.
OverlayWindow::SetupOverlay derives the selection bounds from ClientAreaInScreenSpace, and OverlayWindow::OnLeftButtonUp passes cropRect relative to that client area.

ReparentCropAndLockWindow::CropAndLock reads both GetWindowRect and ClientAreaInScreenSpace, then overrides diffX/diffY for maximized windows with monitor work-area offsets before calculating the crop window position and moving the source HWND to -cropRect.left/-cropRect.top.
ThumbnailCropAndLockWindow::CropAndLock adjusts the same client-relative crop for a DWM thumbnail source rectangle and does not reparent or move the source window.
Existing UI tests cover Win32 and packaged fixture reparent behavior, but the fixture coverage does not appear to exercise maximized Chromium custom-frame windows.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Reparent mode crop coordinates in the selected client coordinate space for maximized Chromium windows
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Reparent mode appears to convert the overlay's client-relative crop rectangle through a maximized-window work-area adjustment before positioning the reparented source HWND. For maximized Chromium/custom-frame windows, that adjustment can shift the displayed pixels away from the selected client region even though input still targets the original source coordinates.
plan: Reproduce with maximized Edge or Chrome and log the selected cropRect from OverlayWindow, GetWindowRect, ClientAreaInScreenSpace, monitor rcWork, and the final SetWindowPos target offset in ReparentCropAndLockWindow.

Remove or narrow the maximized-window special-case offset so Reparent mode uses the actual client-area origin that OverlayWindow used for selection, not a work-area approximation that can diverge for custom-framed browsers.
Keep the Crop And Lock window placement and child clipping rectangle separate from the source HWND offset; verify that the visible region and hit-testing use the same crop origin.
Add regression coverage with a maximized test source whose client origin differs from the window/work-area origin, and extend manual validation to Chromium browsers at common DPI/scaling settings.
verification: Maximize Edge or Chrome, crop a recognizable page region with Reparent mode, and confirm the Crop And Lock window displays exactly the selected pixels.
Click controls inside the cropped window and confirm input still lands on the same visible content.
Repeat with Thumbnail mode to verify no regression.
Run the CropAndLockModuleInterface and CropAndLock builds plus the CropAndLock.UITests reparent scenarios where the local environment supports them.

confidence.rationale: The issue gives a deterministic repro and the source has a focused Reparent-only maximized coordinate branch that matches the symptom, but the exact Chromium frame metrics still need runtime confirmation before implementing.

actions.label: Queue detailed design for Crop And Lock Reparent browser offset

reproduce.version_requirements: PowerToys 0.101.2362 or a current local build with Crop And Lock enabled
prerequisites: Use Windows 11 with Edge or Chrome installed.
Enable Crop And Lock and use Reparent mode, not Thumbnail mode.
Open a browser page with easily identifiable regions, such as a video player or large blocks of text.
steps: 2. Start Crop And Lock Reparent mode.
3. Select a recognizable client-area region in the browser and confirm the crop.
4. Compare the visible pixels in the Crop And Lock window with the selected region.
5. Click a visible element inside the crop and observe whether the input targets the corresponding original browser content.
reproduce.expected_result: The Reparent window shows exactly the selected browser client-area pixels, and click hit-testing targets the same visible content.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create a local Crop And Lock repro page with high-contrast labeled regions, maximize Edge or Chrome, then run Reparent mode while recording the selected crop rectangle, client-area screen origin, window rectangle, monitor work area, and final SetWindowPos offset.

upstream_safety.detail: No comments, labels, assignments, closures, or other public mutations were made to microsoft/PowerToys.
